title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
keyIdea: Carry the largest value seen on the path from the root (maxValue) down a DFS. A node is good when val >= maxValue; pass max(maxValue, val) to its children and add up the counts.

approaches.name: DFS carrying the max so far
approaches.idea: dfs(node, maxValue): count 1 if val >= maxValue, then recurse into both children with max(maxValue, val).
approaches.why: Each node visited once; the stack is as deep as the tree.

quiz.q: Why is one number (maxValue) enough to decide if a node is good?
options: "Nothing on the path is bigger" means val >= the biggest value on the path
Because the tree is a BST
A value equal to the path max is still good (nothing is strictly bigger)
The root has nothing above it, so it must always count as good
INT_MIN is the answer for empty trees
